_note: THE LIVE CODEX RUN (2026-09-08, dogfood rerun 3; entry `e80de7b29ab3d2021`, recorded on build cb838ec). These are the daemon's own exported bytes: Codex CLI 0.153.0 in its TUI under a per-run `CODEX_HOME`, one typed goal, an `exec`/`apply_patch` that added `hello.py`, the harness quit, `goalcup resume` relaunched it on the BOUND thread, `keep going`, and `goalcup seal`. Nothing was scrubbed and no line of it was written by hand. It is the Codex twin of `opencode-live/`: the fixture that measures the CAPTURE rather than the reader, because the three M0 fixtures are transcripts a spike scraped after the fact.
_why_it_is_here: Dogfood fix 7, finding 1. This run FAILED before the fix, on `unexplained_seal_file` for the one file it wrote. `connectors/codex-cli/manifest.toml` classes `exec` as both a write and a shell tool — correctly, since Codex has one tool and its argument text carries either a shell command or the `apply_patch` DSL — and `attribution.rs` branched `if is_shell { shell rule } else { write rule }`, so `patch_target_paths`, written for this exact payload, was unreachable on every real Codex capture. `hello.py` is `traced` to `exec` here, which is the fix asserted on real bytes rather than on a constructed manifest.
_why_flag_and_not_pass: One finding stands: `placeholder_server_key`. This run's receipt and acknowledgements were signed by the M1 placeholder anchor whose private seed is published in this repository, which is what a development run has and what `goalcup-verify --dev` suppresses. Under `--dev` this trace is `pass` with an EMPTY review queue, which `tests/end_to_end.rs` asserts beside the strict reading. V1-V12 all pass.
_the_manifest_here_is_a_copy: Like `opencode-live/` and unlike the three M0 descriptors, this trace carries the manifest bytes the daemon EXPORTED, because the start receipt binds their digest. They are byte-identical to `connectors/codex-cli/manifest.toml` today. A later change to that file makes `manifest_pin` read `altered` here and adds `manifest_not_pinned`: that is the fixture saying, correctly, that the rules moved after the run. Re-record it rather than editing it.
first_human_message: Create hello.py that prints hello world, then stop.
